title: TimeKAN block: template–harmonic blending
summary: The current standalone TimeKAN-inspired operator combines familiar numerical estimates. It smooths a trend, selects periods from a prefix FFT, averages phase templates, and fits a harmonic projection at the supplied primary period. A fixed rule blends the two seasonal estimates. The animation shows that rule directly; it does not portray the complete frequency-decomposition KAN architecture from the cited paper.

steps.title: Smooth and inspect prefix frequencies
steps.text: Estimate the trend from the selected prefix and use the detrended prefix FFT to obtain candidate periods.

steps.title: Fit two kinds of seasonal estimate
steps.text: Average phase templates at selected periods and separately fit a harmonic projection at primary_period.

steps.title: Apply the implemented fixed blend
steps.text: Combine the template average and harmonic projection using a weight determined by num_bands. No KAN is optimized in this operator.

steps.title: Inspect the checked output
steps.text: Return the smoothed trend, blended seasonal estimate and input-minus-components residual.

parameters.name: num_bands
parameters.effect: Controls the selected template periods and the fixed blend weight 0.35 + 0.1 × min(num_bands, 4), clipped by the implementation.

parameters.name: kan_width
parameters.effect: Maps to max(1, kan_width // 32) harmonics in this operator.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Sets the harmonic projection's period; FFT-selected periods define the separate templates.

parameters.name: fit_scope / train_fraction
parameters.effect: The animation explicitly fits on the first two thirds of the record.

cautions: No KAN coefficients or neural network are fitted by this standalone implementation.
Template and harmonic components can overlap spectrally; the displayed blend is an explicit heuristic.
Prefix fitting and suffix extension do not establish forecast accuracy or causal identification.
The residual is defined from the observed series after forming both named components.

references.title: Huang et al. (2025), TimeKAN: KAN-based Frequency Decomposition Learning Architecture for Long-term Time Series Forecasting

trace_note: Intermediate arrays are computed with the implemented operator helpers. The final trend, season and residual are checked against public decompose(). The animation explains this standalone experimental block; its source architecture is cited for provenance.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.

checks.validation_scope: One deterministic teaching input; no benchmark claim.
